questions.question_text: A Wisconsin licensee represents the seller exclusively. What type of agency is this?
questions.correct_answer: Seller's agent
distractors: Dual agent
Subagent
Transaction broker
questions.explanation: A seller's agent represents only the seller's interests. Since 2015 Wisconsin Act 258 the agency relationship is with the firm, and Wisconsin's categories are client representation, subagency, and — when one firm represents two clients in the same transaction — a multiple representation relationship, with or without designated agency.

questions.question_text: A Wisconsin firm wants to represent both the buyer and the seller in the same transaction. What does the law require?
questions.correct_answer: Written consent of all the firm's clients to a multiple representation relationship
distractors: Verbal consent of both parties before the offer is written
Approval from the firm's supervising broker
Nothing, because Wisconsin prohibits representing both parties
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.134 (2) bars a firm from providing brokerage services in a multiple representation relationship unless all of the firm's clients in it have consented in writing. Designated agency requires a second, separate written consent under s. 452.134 (3) (a), which a client may withdraw in writing at any time. Wisconsin's statutes do not use the term 'dual agency.'

questions.question_text: A listing firm engages another firm to help provide brokerage services for its seller-client. The second firm is acting as a:
questions.correct_answer: Subagent
distractors: Buyer's firm
Designated agent
Multiple representation firm
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.01 (7r) defines a subagent as a firm engaged by a principal firm to provide brokerage services in a transaction but not associated with that principal firm. Under REEB 24.07 (8) (b) 2. a firm may not permit subagency unless its client authorized it in the agency agreement. A subagent owes all parties the s. 452.133 (1) duties but does not owe the principal firm's clients the s. 452.133 (2) client duties.

questions.question_text: Which term does Wisconsin's real estate license law NOT use?
questions.correct_answer: Dual agent
distractors: Subagent
Designated agency
Multiple representation relationship
questions.explanation: Since 2015 Wisconsin Act 258 there is no 'dual agent' in ch. 452. When a firm has agency agreements with two clients in the same transaction, s. 452.01 (5j) calls it a multiple representation relationship, which may use designated agency as defined in s. 452.01 (3w). Subagency is defined at s. 452.01 (7r).

questions.question_text: A firm is in a multiple representation relationship WITHOUT designated agency. What limitation applies?
questions.correct_answer: Neither the firm nor its agents may favor one client over another in negotiations
distractors: The firm must charge both clients the same commission
The firm must withdraw if the clients disagree on price
The firm may not show the property to its buyer-client
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.134 (4) provides that if a client does not consent to designated agency, or withdraws consent, the firm and its licensees may not place the interests of any client ahead of any other in the negotiations. With designated agency, s. 452.134 (3) (b) says the opposite: each designated licensee may give their own client information, opinions, and advice even though it advantages that client over the firm's other client.

questions.question_text: When must a Wisconsin firm give the statutory Disclosure to Customers?
questions.correct_answer: Before negotiating on behalf of a party who is not the firm's client
distractors: At first substantive contact with any party
Within 3 business days of the first showing
At the time the offer to purchase is written
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.135 (1) (a) bars a firm or its licensees from negotiating on behalf of a party who is not the firm's client unless it first provides the written Disclosure to Customers. The companion Disclosure to Clients under s. 452.135 (2) (a) must be given no later than the time the firm enters into the agency agreement.

questions.question_text: A buyer's agent contacts the listing firm about a 1-4 family residential property. When must the buyer agency relationship be disclosed?
questions.correct_answer: At the earlier of the first contact exchanging transaction information, a showing, or any negotiation
distractors: Only when the buyer's agent submits a written offer
Within 48 hours after the first showing
Only if the listing firm asks who the agent represents
questions.explanation: Wis. Admin. Code REEB 24.07 (8) (a) 2. requires a licensee acting for a buyer of one to 4 family residential real estate, who negotiates directly with the seller or who knows the seller granted a listing firm the exclusive right to sell, to notify the seller or listing firm of the buyer agency relationship at the earlier of first contact where information about the seller or the transaction is exchanged, a showing of the property, or any other negotiation.

questions.question_text: What form must agency disclosure take in Wisconsin?
questions.correct_answer: Written disclosure
distractors: Verbal disclosure is sufficient
Email disclosure is not accepted
No specific form is required
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.135 requires a written disclosure statement — the Disclosure to Customers under sub. (1) and the Disclosure to Clients under sub. (2) — and prints the statutory text the firm must reproduce.

questions.question_text: What must a licensee explain during the agency disclosure?
questions.correct_answer: Their role and duties to all parties
distractors: Only their commission percentage
Only whether they represent buyer or seller
Only the names of other licensees involved
questions.explanation: The statutory disclosures set out the firm's duties: fair and honest brokerage services, reasonable skill and care, accurate market information on request, written disclosure of material adverse facts, protection of confidentiality, safeguarding of trust funds, and objective presentation of contract proposals when negotiating.

questions.question_text: A licensee at an open house is working with a prospective buyer who is not the firm's client. What triggers the Disclosure to Customers?
questions.correct_answer: Negotiating on that person's behalf
distractors: Any substantive conversation about the property
The buyer entering the property
The buyer asking about the asking price
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.135 (1) (a) ties the Disclosure to Customers to negotiating on behalf of a non-client. 'Negotiate' is defined in s. 452.01 (5m) and includes acting as an intermediary in communications between parties, completing board-approved forms at a party's request, and presenting other parties' proposals with a general explanation — but expressly not merely giving advice or opinions, or showing real estate.

questions.question_text: Under Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1) (c), which material adverse facts must a firm disclose?
questions.correct_answer: Those the firm knows and the party does not know or cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation
distractors: Every material adverse fact the firm knows or should know
Only those the firm discovers in its own inspection
Only those the seller discloses to the firm
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1) (c) is the duty to timely disclose in writing all material adverse facts the firm knows and that the party does not know or cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation, unless disclosure is prohibited by law. The separate obligation to go looking for them is the reasonably competent and diligent inspection required by REEB 24.07 (1).

questions.question_text: What inspection duty does Wis. Admin. Code REEB 24.07 (1) place on a licensee?
questions.correct_answer: A reasonably competent and diligent inspection of accessible areas to detect observable material adverse facts
distractors: A professional home inspection before any listing is signed
No inspection duty — that belongs to a third-party inspector
An inspection only when the client requests one in writing
questions.explanation: REEB 24.07 (1) (a) requires inspection of accessible areas of the structure and the immediately surrounding areas. Under (1) (d) it does not require operating mechanical equipment, opening panels, moving property, climbing a ladder, or retaining third-party inspectors. A listing licensee must inspect before the listing contract is executed and must ask the seller for a written response about the property's condition.

questions.question_text: Which best describes a 'material adverse fact' under Wis. Stat. s. 452.01 (5g)?
questions.correct_answer: An adverse fact significant enough to affect a party's decision to contract or the terms
distractors: Any condition that reduces the property's value
Any fact a buyer asks about directly
Any defect a licensed home inspector would report
questions.explanation: Wisconsin uses two nested terms. An 'adverse fact' under s. 452.01 (1e) is a condition significantly and adversely affecting value, significantly reducing structural integrity, or presenting a significant health risk — or information that a party cannot or will not meet its obligations. It becomes a 'material' adverse fact under s. 452.01 (5g) only when it is significant enough to affect a party's decision to enter into the contract, or its terms.

questions.question_text: A listing agent learns the property has recurring flooding in the basement. What must they do?
questions.correct_answer: Disclose this material adverse fact to all parties
distractors: Only mention it if the buyer asks directly
Let the seller decide whether to disclose
Include it only in the condition report
questions.explanation: Recurring flooding is a material adverse fact. Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1) (c) and REEB 24.07 (2) require the licensee to disclose it to each party in writing and in a timely fashion. The duty is not limited to the condition of the property, and under s. 452.133 (6) it cannot be waived.

questions.question_text: The material adverse facts disclosure duty in Wisconsin is described as:
questions.correct_answer: An affirmative duty that applies to all licensees
distractors: A passive duty triggered only by buyer questions
A duty that applies only to listing agents
A duty that applies only to dual agents
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1) (c) makes the material adverse facts duty affirmative and owed to every party the firm provides brokerage services to, regardless of whom the firm represents. Section 452.133 (6) makes it non-waivable.

questions.question_text: Which duty does a Wisconsin firm owe ONLY to a client, and not to every party?
questions.correct_answer: The duty to loyally represent the client's interests
distractors: The duty to keep information confidential
The duty to provide brokerage services with reasonable skill and care
The duty to safeguard trust funds
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1) lists the duties owed to all parties: honest and fair service, reasonable skill and care, written disclosure of material adverse facts, confidentiality, accurate market information on request, safeguarding trust funds, and objective presentation of proposals when negotiating. Section 452.133 (2) adds the client-only duties: loyalty, information and advice on request, disclosure of all material information, fulfilling the agency agreement and the client's orders within its scope, and negotiating for the client.

questions.question_text: A listing firm is working with a buyer who is not its client. Which duty does the firm owe that buyer?
questions.correct_answer: The duty to keep the buyer's information confidential
distractors: The duty to loyally represent the buyer's interests
The duty to negotiate on the buyer's behalf
No duty beyond basic honesty
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1) (d) places confidentiality among the duties owed to all parties, and the statutory Disclosure to Customers in s. 452.135 (1) (a) says so plainly: 'The duty to protect your confidentiality.' What a customer does not receive are the s. 452.133 (2) client duties — loyalty, advice on request, and negotiation.

questions.question_text: What duties does a Wisconsin firm owe a customer under Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1)?
questions.correct_answer: Honesty and fairness, reasonable skill and care, confidentiality, disclosure of material adverse facts, and safeguarding trust funds
distractors: Only honesty and fair dealing
The same full duties owed to a client
Only the duty to present written offers
questions.explanation: Section 452.133 (1) owes every party seven duties: honest and fair brokerage services; reasonable skill and care; timely written disclosure of material adverse facts; confidentiality; accurate market information on request; safeguarding of trust funds; and, when negotiating, objective and unbiased presentation of contract proposals. Confidentiality is on that list — a common trap for candidates who studied a national text.

questions.question_text: Under Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (2) (c), what must a firm do with its client's instructions?
questions.correct_answer: Fulfill orders within the scope of the agency agreement that are consistent with its other legal duties
distractors: Obey every instruction the client gives
Follow instructions only if the client puts them in writing
Follow instructions only with the supervising broker's approval
questions.explanation: Wisconsin's client-duty list is closed and contains no duty of 'obedience.' Section 452.133 (2) (c) is the duty to fulfill any obligation required by the agency agreement, and any order of the client that is within the scope of that agreement, that is not inconsistent with another duty the firm has under ch. 452 or any other law.

questions.question_text: A listing firm learns that the buyer — a customer, not a client — is pre-approved for far more than the offer price. May the firm tell its seller-client?
questions.correct_answer: No, that is confidential customer information
distractors: Yes, the duty of disclosure to the client requires it
Yes, if the buyer's firm agrees
Yes, but only after the offer is accepted
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.133 (1) (d) owes confidentiality to all parties, including customers, and it continues after the transaction is complete. REEB 24.07 (2) carries the mirror-image example as an official Note: unless the seller specifically authorizes it, a licensee may not tell a prospective buyer the actual minimum price the seller will accept.
